summary: A reinforced-concrete tower of 1909 on a cliff at Cap-Chat, Gaspésie, with a light since 1871; the tower is closed and the grounds are open.

structures.note: Square reinforced-concrete tower with a round red lantern. CCG list 9.5 m (white square tower with red top); LighthouseFriends and the register give about 10 m
First tower: square wooden, dwelling built in. The register says it was demolished in 1961; LighthouseFriends says a second wooden tower replaced it in 1875

access.note: Grounds and the Jardin des Brumes are open; the tower is closed (register; LighthouseFriends). The keeper's house is described as a tea room (register) and as rentable for overnight stays (LighthouseFriends, routedesphares).

stay.note: Former keeper's house rentable for overnight stays (LighthouseFriends; routedesphares). The register describes a tea room. Check with the operator before planning a stay.

facts.agency: Sources differ: the register says the municipality keeps the light lit and the Musée Germain-Lemieux runs the site; LighthouseFriends says the Parc récréotouristique du rocher Cap-Chat owns and manages it; the non-profit Les gardiens du Phare Cap-Chat works to preserve it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and LighthouseFriends give 1909. routedesphares gives 1911 for the present tower. The Department of Marine report for the year to 31 March 1910 says the new tower had already been erected, which supports 1909.
The 1910 Department report describes one flash every three seconds; the current CCG list gives Fl W 6s. No source read here dates the change.

The register says the first tower (1871) was demolished in 1961, when its 1919 fog-signal shelter was replaced. LighthouseFriends says a second wooden tower replaced the first in 1875. The register's 'first' tower may be that second one (our inference). Unresolved; the story reports both.

LighthouseFriends says the Fresnel lens was deactivated in 2007, leaving a privately maintained emergency light. The Coast Guard list gives the main light Fl W 6s, operating 24 h, marked Private aid, with an emergency light Fl(6) W 15s. The register says the light is still operated by the Canadian Coast Guard and kept lit by the municipality. Unresolved; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Shape: light-station headings. Keepers: names and years come only from LighthouseFriends. LighthouseFriends' text has lost its accented letters (the bytes are invalid), so the accents on Côté, Treflé, Aurèle, François and Tréflé are restored one per lost letter. They are plausible but not confirmed by a second source; left as restored and flagged here. Matched by position and checked on the page image: the 1923-24 Cape Chat dwelling line (printed p.30, scan p.37, 1925v61i5p28_1773) and the 1918 casualty row for the Cape Corso (printed p.72, scan p.71, 1919v54i8p21_1432: the OCR prints 'Cape Coirso' and 'Nlay 15'; the page shows 'Cape Corso, 117396, Greenock' on the row with 'On May 15 stranded in vicinity of cape Chat'). The 1914 salvage entry is in Appendix 15 (Quebec Salvage and Wrecking Company), printed p.345, scan p.352, not a log. Chronology conflicts stated in the story: the register says the first tower (1871) was demolished in 1961; LighthouseFriends says a second wooden tower replaced it in 1875. Status conflicts stated: LighthouseFriends says the Fresnel lens was deactivated in 2007; the CCG list gives Fl W 6s operating 24 h; the register says it is still operated by the Canadian Coast Guard and kept lit by the municipality. Fog-shelter date (1918 diaphone, LighthouseFriends; 1919 shelter, register) and tower height (CCG 9.5 m, about 10 m in the register and LighthouseFriends) are both recorded. Miffonis appears in the 1908-1910 Marine reports at other stations; the design attribution is the register's. The WWII U-boat claim (LighthouseFriends, which gives no source) was removed from the story as unsourced. Management conflicts: the register (Musée Germain-Lemieux), LighthouseFriends (Parc récréotouristique du rocher Cap-Chat), the non-profit Les gardiens (preservation). Gardiens du Phare is an organisation; the keepers are named only as LighthouseFriends names them. Keepers after 1960 are named only as the published source gives them, with no personal detail. No photos were added; the record's Commons photo was not checked for licence.
